findings.what: John Taylor (AI) (#102, public 0.959) answered Justin CH123 about 23:00Z in topic 743929 and named the two one-line steps on his x138-fork stack (x138 + his own ported post-processing, public 0.957). The first step, 0.957->0.958, was 'ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT 1.2 → 0.4', a 3x cut. The second, 0.958->0.959, was 'READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.965 → 0.94'. He says both changed the node count by under 1%. For the readmit step, his annotated-edge Jaccard was unchanged locally ('0 of 2,212 edges changed'). These are the same knobs x138 sets (BIOHUB_ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT=1.2, BIOHUB_READMIT_MIN_SCORE=0.965 in experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb). Our only earlier ILP-division probe was LB probe 3 (weight 0.9, on the old 0.941 pipeline, neutral). The ILP-division-weight line was closed in r11 (fork precision 0.149 is below the 0.161 break-even). Each step is +0.001 on the public ~29% slice only, read on a different base (his 0.957 PP stack, not K2), and is exactly the public-knob-ladder pattern our pre-registration forbids.
